LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only sources the PKGBUILD file without executing functions like `pkgver()`, `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()`. In this PKGBUILD, the global/top-level scope only contains standard variable definitions (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `makedepends`, `checkdepends`, `optdepends`, `options`, `_ref`, `source`, `sha256sums`). There are no command substitutions, network requests, file modifications, `eval`, `base64`, `curl`, `wget`, or other potentially dangerous operations at the top level. All code that could execute maliciously (like the `prepare()`, `build()`, `check()`, and `package()` functions using `zig build`, `rsvg-convert`, `desktop-file-validate`, and file installations) is inside function definitions that won't run during `--printsrcinfo`.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>PKGBUILD is safe for makepkg --printsrcinfo</summary>
</security_assessment>
